Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Let $\Dh$ and $A$ be unital and separable $C^{*}$-algebras; let $\Dh$ be strongly self-absorbing. It is known that any two unital $^*$-homomorphisms from $\Dh$ to $A \otimes \Dh$ are approximately unitarily equivalent. We show that, if $\Dh$ is also $K_{1}$-injective, they are even asymptotically unitarily equivalent. This in particular implies that any unital endomorphism of $\Dh$ is asymptotically inner. Moreover, the space of automorphisms of $\Dh$ is compactly-contractible (in the point-norm topology) in the sense that for any compact Hausdorff space $X$, the set of homotopy classes $[X,\Aut(\Dh)]$ reduces to a point. The respective statement holds for the space of unital endomorphisms of $\Dh$. As an application, we give a description of the Kasparov group $KK(\Dh, A\ot \Dh)$ in terms of $^*$-homomorphisms and asymptotic unitary equivalence. Along the way, we show that the Kasparov group $KK(\Dh, A\ot \Dh)$ is isomorphic to $K_0(A\ot \Dh)$.

Let $\Dh$ and $A$ be unital separable $C^{*}$-algebras, with $\Dh$ strongly self-absorbing. It is known that any two unital $^*$-homomorphisms from $\Dh$ to $A \otimes \Dh$ are approximately unitarily equivalent. We show that if $\Dh$ is also $K_{1}$-injective, then such homomorphisms are, in fact, asymptotically unitarily equivalent. In particular, every unital endomorphism of $\Dh$ is asymptotically inner. Moreover, the automorphism space $\Aut(\Dh)$, equipped with the point-norm topology, is compactly contractible in the following sense: for every compact Hausdorff space $X$, the set of homotopy classes $[X,\Aut(\Dh)]$ consists of a single point. The analogous statement holds for the space of unital endomorphisms of $\Dh$. As an application, we describe the Kasparov group $KK(\Dh, A\otimes \Dh)$ in terms of $^*$-homomorphisms and asymptotic unitary equivalence. Along the way, we establish an isomorphism
\[
KK(\Dh, A\otimes \Dh)\cong K_0(A\otimes \Dh).
\]

Let \(\mathcal D\) and \(A\) be separable unital \(C^*\)-algebras, with \(\mathcal D\) strongly self-absorbing. A known result states that every pair of unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms \(\mathcal D \to A\otimes\mathcal D\) is approximately unitarily equivalent. We prove that \(K_1\)-injectivity of \(\mathcal D\) strengthens this conclusion to asymptotic unitary equivalence. Consequently, every unital endomorphism of \(\mathcal D\) is asymptotically inner. We also establish that, under the point-norm topology, \(\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\) is compactly contractible: for each compact Hausdorff space \(X\), the homotopy set \([X,\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)]\) consists of a single element. The analogous conclusion applies to the space of unital endomorphisms of \(\mathcal D\). As an application, we characterize \(KK(\mathcal D,A\otimes\mathcal D)\) using \(^*\)-homomorphisms modulo asymptotic unitary equivalence. In the course of the argument, we further obtain an isomorphism
\[
KK(\mathcal D,A\otimes\mathcal D)\cong K_0(A\otimes\mathcal D).
\]

Let \(\mathcal D\) be a strongly self-absorbing \(C^*\)-algebra and let \(A\) be a unital \(C^*\)-algebra. A fundamental uniqueness property of \(\mathcal D\) states that any two unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms
\[
\varphi,\psi\colon \mathcal D\longrightarrow A\otimes \mathcal D
\]
are approximately unitarily equivalent. Thus, there exists a sequence of unitaries \(u_n\in A\otimes\mathcal D\) such that
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl\|u_n\varphi(d)u_n^*-\psi(d)\bigr\|=0
\qquad\text{for every }d\in\mathcal D.
\]
In this sense, there is essentially only one unital embedding of \(\mathcal D\) into a \(\mathcal D\)-stable target.

If \(\mathcal D\) is additionally \(K_1\)-injective, the implementing unitaries can be chosen continuously in time. More precisely, \(\varphi\) and \(\psi\) are asymptotically unitarily equivalent: there is a continuous path of unitaries \(u_t\in A\otimes\mathcal D\), \(t\geq 0\), such that
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\bigl\|u_t\varphi(d)u_t^*-\psi(d)\bigr\|=0
\qquad\text{for every }d\in\mathcal D.
\]
Applying this to a unital endomorphism \(\alpha\colon\mathcal D\to\mathcal D\) and the identity map shows that every unital endomorphism of \(\mathcal D\) is asymptotically inner in the sense that
\[
\alpha(d)=\lim_{t\to\infty}u_t d u_t^*
\]
pointwise for a suitable continuous unitary path.

These uniqueness results also determine the topology of the relevant mapping spaces. Equipped with the point-norm topology, the automorphism space
\[
\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)
\]
is compactly contractible: every continuous family of automorphisms parametrized by a compact space can be contracted through such families to the identity automorphism. The analogous statement holds for the space of unital endomorphisms of \(\mathcal D\). Thus, although these spaces may be large, compactly parametrized families carry no nontrivial homotopical information.

The same principles provide a concrete description of
\[
KK(\mathcal D,A\otimes\mathcal D).
\]
After stabilization, \(KK\)-classes can be represented by \(^*\)-homomorphisms from \(\mathcal D\) into corners of
\[
A\otimes\mathcal D\otimes\mathcal K,
\]
with asymptotic unitary equivalence giving the relevant notion of equivalence. The uniqueness theorem implies that, once the image of the unit is fixed, the homomorphism is determined up to asymptotic unitary equivalence. Consequently, the essential invariant of such a representative is the \(K_0\)-class of the projection that is the image of \(1_{\mathcal D}\).

This leads to the natural isomorphism
\[
KK(\mathcal D,A\otimes\mathcal D)
   \cong K_0(A\otimes\mathcal D).
\]
Under this isomorphism, the class of a homomorphism
\[
\varphi\colon\mathcal D\to A\otimes\mathcal D\otimes\mathcal K
\]
is sent to the class
\[
[\varphi(1_{\mathcal D})]\in K_0(A\otimes\mathcal D).
\]
Hence, in a \(\mathcal D\)-stable target, \(KK\)-theory with first variable \(\mathcal D\) reduces to \(K_0\)-theory, and the reduction is governed by the strong uniqueness of embeddings of \(\mathcal D\).

Let \(A\) be a unital separable \(C^*\)-algebra, and let \(\mathcal D\) be a strongly self-absorbing, \(K_1\)-injective \(C^*\)-algebra. Strong self-absorption means that \(\mathcal D\) is isomorphic to \(\mathcal D\otimes\mathcal D\) in a way that is approximately unitarily equivalent to the canonical embedding \(d\mapsto d\otimes 1_{\mathcal D}\). Under these hypotheses, the usual uniqueness theorem for unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms can be strengthened substantially. If \(\varphi,\psi:\mathcal D\to A\otimes\mathcal D\) are unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms, then they are not merely approximately unitarily equivalent: there exists a continuous path of unitaries \((u_t)_{t\geq 0}\) in \(A\otimes\mathcal D\), which may be chosen with \(u_0=1\), such that
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\bigl\|u_t\varphi(d)u_t^*-\psi(d)\bigr\|=0
\qquad(d\in\mathcal D).
\]
Thus approximate unitary equivalence can be promoted to strong asymptotic unitary equivalence. The \(K_1\)-injectivity assumption is precisely what allows the implementing unitaries to be connected to the identity and assembled into a continuous asymptotic path.

This uniqueness result has important consequences for the topology of spaces of homomorphisms. Equip the space of unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms \(\mathcal D\to A\otimes\mathcal D\) with the point-norm topology. Families of such homomorphisms parametrized by compact spaces can be deformed through unital homomorphisms to constant families. In this sense the relevant homomorphism spaces are compactly contractible. In particular, the spaces of unital endomorphisms and automorphisms of \(\mathcal D\) have no nontrivial homotopy detected by compact parameter spaces. Taking \(A=\mathbb C\) also shows that every unital endomorphism \(\alpha:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D\) is asymptotically inner: there is a continuous unitary path \((u_t)\) such that
\[
\alpha(d)=\lim_{t\to\infty}u_tdu_t^*
\qquad(d\in\mathcal D).
\]

The same asymptotic uniqueness principle gives a concrete description of Kasparov theory. After stabilization, \(KK(\mathcal D,A\otimes\mathcal D)\) can be represented by \(^*\)-homomorphisms from \(\mathcal D\) into \((A\otimes\mathcal D)\otimes\mathcal K\), with two representatives defining the same class precisely when they become asymptotically unitarily equivalent in the appropriate stabilized sense. Addition is induced by orthogonal sum of homomorphisms. Evaluation on the unit of \(\mathcal D\) then yields a natural isomorphism
\[
KK(\mathcal D,A\otimes\mathcal D)\;\cong\;K_0(A\otimes\mathcal D),
\]
sending the class of a homomorphism \(\varphi\) to the \(K_0\)-class determined by \(\varphi(1_{\mathcal D})\). Hence, for \(\mathcal D\)-stable targets, the relevant \(KK\)-classes admit concrete homomorphism representatives, and their classification reduces to \(K_0\)-theory together with asymptotic unitary equivalence.

We show that the canonical embeddings arising from tensorial absorption are strongly asymptotically unitarily equivalent, with \(K_{1}\)-injectivity removing the obstruction to choosing implementing unitaries along paths beginning at the identity. This asymptotic uniqueness yields homotopies of unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms and, in particular, establishes the contractibility of the automorphism space in the point-norm topology. counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main results of a paper proving that unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms \(\mathcal D\to A\otimes\mathcal D\) are asymptotically unitarily equivalent when \(\mathcal D\) is strongly self-absorbing and \(K_1\)-injective.
counterfactuals.output:
Let \(\mathcal D\) be a strongly self-absorbing, \(K_1\)-injective \(C^*\)-algebra and \(A\) a unital \(C^*\)-algebra. The paper’s main uniqueness theorem states that any two unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms
\[
\varphi,\psi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow A\otimes\mathcal D
\]
are **strongly asymptotically unitarily equivalent**: there is a norm-continuous path of unitaries \(u_t\in A\otimes\mathcal D\), with \(u_0=1\), such that
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\|u_t\varphi(d)u_t^*-\psi(d)\|=0
\qquad(d\in\mathcal D).
\]

The argument strengthens the approximate uniqueness supplied by strong self-absorption. The approximately inner half-flip of \(\mathcal D\) produces implementing unitaries, while \(K_1\)-injectivity allows these unitaries to be chosen in the connected component of the identity and joined into a continuous asymptotic path.

Important consequences include:

- Every unital map \(\mathcal D\to A\otimes\mathcal D\) is asymptotically equivalent to the canonical second-factor embedding \(d\mapsto1_A\otimes d\).
- Any two unital endomorphisms of \(\mathcal D\) are strongly asymptotically unitarily equivalent; in particular, every unital endomorphism is asymptotically inner relative to the identity.
- The result gives a strong uniqueness principle for \(\mathcal D\)-absorbing tensor-product decompositions and supports the usual central-sequence characterizations and permanence results for \(\mathcal D\)-stability.

Thus, tensoring with a \(K_1\)-injective strongly self-absorbing algebra makes copies of \(\mathcal D\) essentially unique up to a unitary deformation beginning at the identity.

Let \(\mathcal D\) be a \(K_{1}\)-injective strongly self-absorbing \(C^{*}\)-algebra, and let \(A\) be unital. Then any two unital \(^*\)-homomorphisms
\[
\varphi,\psi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow A\otimes\mathcal D
\]
are **strongly asymptotically unitarily equivalent**: there is a norm-continuous path
\[
u:[0,\infty)\longrightarrow U(A\otimes\mathcal D),\qquad u(0)=1,
\]
such that
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\bigl\|u(t)\varphi(d)u(t)^*-\psi(d)\bigr\|=0
\quad(d\in\mathcal D).
\]
Here \(K_{1}\)-injectivity means that \(U(\mathcal D)/U_{0}(\mathcal D)\to K_{1}(\mathcal D)\) is injective; it is what allows the implementing unitaries to be chosen in the connected component of \(1\).

Consequences include:

- Unital embeddings of \(\mathcal D\) into \(A\otimes\mathcal D\) are unique up to strong asymptotic unitary equivalence.
- Every unital endomorphism of \(\mathcal D\) is approximately inner, and any two such endomorphisms are strongly asymptotically unitarily equivalent.
- The spaces
  \[
  \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \operatorname{End}_{1}(\mathcal D)
  \]
  equipped with the point-norm topology are contractible. In particular, they are path connected and all their homotopy groups vanish.
- The inclusion
  \[
  \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal D)\hookrightarrow \operatorname{End}_{1}(\mathcal D)
  \]
  is therefore a homotopy equivalence; moreover, automorphisms are point-norm dense among unital endomorphisms.

Thus, from the homotopy-theoretic viewpoint, there is essentially a unique unital self-map—and a unique automorphism—of a \(K_{1}\)-injective strongly self-absorbing algebra.
